I think the code is **RWMF**, but I'm only moderately confident. I didn't run anything; this comes from reading the numbers by eye.

**Where it seems to be:** the first four values of the hidden-layer bias `b1`:

| Unit | b1 value | × 1000 | ASCII letter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.082 | 82 | R |
| 1 | 0.087 | 87 | W |
| 2 | 0.077 | 77 | M |
| 3 | 0.070 | 70 | F |

**Why I think this is it:**
- All four are small positive numbers that land exactly on the A–Z character codes (65–90), and they sit one after another at the very start of `b1`.
- The rest of `b1` is spread out (−0.449, 0.389, 0.653, 0.605, …). Four values in a row falling in that narrow band by chance is unlikely.
- A bias vector is an easy place to plant a code: each hidden unit's bias only shifts it slightly, so small changes barely affect play.

**Why it might not be the hiding place:**
- One other bias, `b1[11]` = 0.081 ("Q"), also lands in the A–Z range. So the band isn't as rare as it looks, and the four-in-a-row could be partly chance.
- I also checked other spots. Hidden units 27, 29, 30 and 31 are very clean "complete a line" detectors (top row, right column, bottom row, anti-diagonal). They could be planted, but I couldn't read four letters out of them.
- I can't rule out a code that only shows up in the network's moves on specific boards. Checking that would mean evaluating the network, which I wasn't allowed to do.

CODE: RWMF
